description: Schema for job posting pages covering both listing (search/browse) pages and individual job detail pages across job boards, career portals, and company career sites.

contexts.listing: Used when extracting multiple job cards from a search results or listing page.
contexts.detail: Used when extracting a single job's full details from its dedicated page.

job_title.description: The full title of the job position as displayed.

job_url.description: The canonical URL to the job posting page.

company_name.description: The name of the hiring company or organization. May be an institution, NGO, UN agency, or government body.

location.description: The job location as shown on the site. May be a city, region, country, or 'Remote'. Normalize to 'City, Region, Country' when possible.

salary.description: Salary or compensation shown on the listing card. Extract as structured object with min_amount, max_amount, currency (code/symbol), and period (year/month/hour) when available. May be null.
salary.normalization: Extract numerical values. Identify currency by code (e.g. GBP, USD) and period (year, month, hour). Set to null if not shown.

employment_type.description: The employment type as shown (e.g. 'Permanent, full-time', 'Contract', 'Part-time'). May be null.

posted_date.description: The date the job was posted. Normalize to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) when possible.
posted_date.normalization: Convert to ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Resolve relative dates (e.g. '3 days ago') using the snapshot date.

application_deadline.description: The closing/deadline date for applications. Normalize to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

country.description: Country of the job location, used on sites that separate country from city/region.

tags.description: Technology or category tags associated with the job (e.g. ['React', 'Remote', 'Senior']).

job_description.description: Short description or teaser text shown on the listing card.

qualifications.description: Key qualification requirements shown on the listing card.

apply_url.description: Direct application URL, when distinct from job_url.

company_logo_url.description: URL of the company's logo image as shown on the listing card.

job_id.description: Internal job identifier used by the site.

salary.description: Full salary or compensation details from the job detail page. Structured object with min_amount, max_amount, currency (name, code, symbol), and period. May also carry flat fields salary_min, salary_max, salary_currency, salary_period.
salary.normalization: Extract min/max numerical values, currency code and symbol, and period. Set to null if not advertised.

salary_range.description: Salary range as a human-readable string when a structured object is not available.
salary_range.normalization: Use format '$X–$Y per year' or equivalent with currency and period.

employment_type.description: Full employment type from the detail page (e.g. 'Permanent, full-time', 'Contract', 'consultant_not_staff_member').

job_description.description: Full job description text from the detail page.

responsibilities.description: List of job responsibilities or duties.

qualifications.description: List of required qualifications, often structured by sub-category (education, experience, languages).

minimum_qualifications.description: Minimum qualifications required (used by Google Careers).

benefits.description: List of employee benefits (e.g. pension, health, parking).

posted_date.description: Date the job was posted. Normalize to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

application_deadline.description: Deadline for applications. Normalize to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

apply_url.description: Direct URL to submit an application, when distinct from job_url.

tags.description: Technology or category tags associated with the job.

skills.description: Specific skills listed for the role.

duration.description: Contract or role duration. May be a string ('Permanent') or structured object with start/end dates.

department.description: The team or department hiring for the role.

job_experience_level.description: Experience level label used by the site (e.g. 'Director+').

discipline.description: Academic or scientific discipline(s) of the position.

academic_discipline.description: Academic discipline categories used by Times Higher Education.

language_requirements.description: Language skills required for the role.

remuneration.description: Structured remuneration details for contract roles (e.g. daily fee, currency, max days/total).

job_id.description: Internal job identifier used by the site.

company_logo_url.description: URL of the company's logo image.

company_overview.description: Company background description included in the job posting.

ideal_candidate.description: Description of the ideal candidate profile.

working_hours.description: Expected working hours or schedule details.

about_the_role.description: Narrative description of the role (Reed-specific section).

about_the_job.description: Overview of the job narrative (Google Careers section).

about_company.description: Company background section from the job detail page.

requirements.description: Free-text requirements section (used on some sites before structured qualification fields).

what_we_offer.description: What the organization offers to the candidate (benefits, culture, mission).

theme.description: Thematic category of the humanitarian job (e.g. 'Health', 'Coordination').

office.description: Specific office or institute location within the organization.

assessment.description: Description of the candidate evaluation/assessment process.

export_control_requirement.description: Export control compliance requirement (e.g. US Person requirement).

about_unu.description: About the United Nations University boilerplate.

about_office_institute.description: Description of the specific UNU office or institute.

category.description: Single job category string (GitHub detail page).

compensation_range.description: Compensation range as a human-readable string (GitHub).

normalization_rules.salary: Extract min_amount and max_amount as numbers. Identify currency by ISO 4217 code (e.g. GBP, USD, EUR) and period (year, month, hour). Store null for fields not present.
normalization_rules.salary_range: Format as a human-readable string, e.g. '$90,000–$135,000/year'. Use currency symbol when available.
normalization_rules.posted_date: Convert to ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Resolve relative expressions (e.g. '3 days ago') using the snapshot date.
normalization_rules.expected_start_date: Convert to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) if a date is given; otherwise retain normalized string (e.g. 'as_soon_as_possible').
normalization_rules.location: Normalize to 'City, Region, Country' when possible. For fully remote roles use 'Remote'. Retain the site's original value if normalization is ambiguous.
normalization_rules.country: Use the ISO country name or code as provided by the site.
normalization_rules.employment_type: Retain the site's original string. Do not normalize across sites.
normalization_rules.job_url: Return the full absolute URL. Resolve relative URLs against the site origin.

notes: The 'salary' field supersedes the earlier 'salary_range' string field. Use 'salary' as a structured object wherever possible; use 'salary_range' only for Google Careers which does not expose structured salary data.
Fields under 'listing_fields' and 'detail_fields' are all optional; their presence depends on the source site and what is visible on the page.
'company_name' is required on most sites but may be absent on GitHub (where the company is always GitHub) — in that case it need not be extracted unless visible.
'location' is required on most sites but is not present in UNJobs listing pages (only job_title, company_name, and job_url are available).
Some sites (e.g. EuroBrussels, ReliefWeb) use 'application_deadline' rather than 'closing_date'; both refer to the same concept and should be stored under 'application_deadline'.
